title: Apple Launching Two More New Products This Friday - MacRumors
text:
Monday November 9, 2026 4:19 am PST by Tim Hardwick

The Apple launches keep coming! The company is set to release two new products on Friday, November 13: the all-new Apple HomeView and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, both of which have been available to pre-order since mid-October. 

- Apple HomeView: Apple's new smart home display, powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, for entertainment and managing the home. Available in tabletop and wall-mounted models, it can recognize up to six users by face, each with a personalized Home Screen. The HomeView is priced at $299.
- Apple TV 4K: adds Siri AI, the A19 chip, an updated Siri Remote with Find My, and support for four-speaker surround sound with HomePod mini 2. The Apple TV 4K comes with 128GB of storage and is priced at $299.

Both products were announced on October 13 alongside the HomePod mini 2, which launched October 30. 

As things stand, HomeView will not be sold in the European Union because Siri AI is currently unavailable on iOS in the region due to regulatory constraints. Apple has said it is "working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," but has provided no timeline for EU availability.

title: Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature - Apple
text:
# Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature 

 New accessibility feature debuts Friday, November 13, with the streaming premiere of Being Heumann 

 Sign Language, the new accessibility feature on the Apple TV app, debuts with the global streaming premiere of the film Being Heumann on November 13. 

Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app that gives viewers the option to watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation. 1 The feature will be available on Friday, November 13, alongside the global streaming premiere of Being Heumann, a film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, on Apple TV. 

In addition to Being Heumann, interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will be available for the movie F1. Later this year, Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow, with more Apple Original titles to come. When turned on in Apple TV app settings, the Sign Language option will appear on supported Apple Original titles.

...

## New Ways to Discover Titles with Sign Language 

Titles with sign language interpretation will be labeled with a Sign Language icon, making it easy to know when the option is available. Viewers can enable the feature in Apple TV app settings, then press the Sign Language button while watching. Search will also make it easier to find titles that feature sign language with simple phrases like “with ASL.”

...

Being Heumann premieres globally on Apple TV on Friday, November 13. Viewers can add Being Heumann to their watchlist on Apple TV.

title: Top Stories: Apple Product Launches, iOS 27.3 Beta, and More - MacRumors
text:
Apple is still rocking and rolling a week into November, with five new products having launched this week and two more still on tap for next week.

 Things are also moving forward on the software side with Apple releasing the first betas of iOS 27.3 and related updates, bringing a number of tweaks and new features. We're also looking ahead to new products coming in the first half of 2027, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more!

...

### Apple Launched Five New Products This Week

Apple released five new products on Friday, November 6, following pre-orders that opened last week, including its first touchscreen MacBook Pro models.

 The following new products are now available:

- iPad mini with OLED display and A20 Pro chip
- iMac with M6 chip
- 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
- 14-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen
- 16-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen

Apple's HomeView smart home hub and updated Apple TV 4K box will follow next week on Friday, November 13. 

### Everything New in the iOS 27.3 Beta

Apple this week started testing iOS 27.3, the biggest update to iOS 27 since it launched in September. iOS 27.3 includes some features Apple showed off earlier this year, and it adds all-new capabilities.

 Among the changes in the update are Safari tweaks with a new Vertical Tabs layout option plus an Adaptive Dark Mode feature for websites that don't offer their own dark mode option, Siri AI improvements, an expansion of new iPhone Duo StandBy features to other iPhone models, and more.

The revamped Health app that was in the 27.2 beta for testing but removed prior to the public release has returned in 27.3 and will be seeing a public launch before the end of the year.

title: Everything coming from Apple in November 2026 | Macworld
text:
Apple should finally be done announcing new hardware for 2026, but there’s still plenty to be released this month. We’ve got the new MacBook Pro with PROLED, M6 iMac, M6 MacBook Pro, HomeView, and Apple TV 4K that were all announced in October.

There’s some exciting software, too. We expect the OS 27.3 updates to bring more new features, including Audio Intelligence to the Apple Watch series 12 and Ultra 4, as well and the new Health app and perhaps a few other new capabilities. And naturally, we’ll get new Apple TV+ shows and Apple Arcade games, as we do every month. Here’s what we can expect from Apple in November 2026.

## New hardware

Apple isn’t expected to announce any new hardware in November, but a lot of the products announced in October don’t actually ship until this month. Here’s what we have on the way.

MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display: The new tandem-OLED MacBook Pro with touch support and the Dynamic Island is shipping on November 6.

M6 iMac: Apple finally updated the iMac with a new processor, though nothing else has changed. It ships on November 6 as well.

iPad mini with OLED: The new iPad mini gets a big upgrade, with an OLED display and an A20 Pro processor. It arrives on November 6, too.

HomeView: Announced last month, the HomeView is the first truly new-category product from Apple in a long time. It doesn’t ship until November 13, so there haven’t even been any reviews yet.

Apple TV 4K (4th gen): The new Apple TV 4K box has a faster processor for Siri AI, built-in microphones, and a remote that has a speaker for Find My. It arrives on November 13.

...

OS 27.3: Apple’s big OS 27 software updates aren’t done yet—there are still a few significant features to come. Among them are a new redesigned Health app, further enhancements to Siri AI, support for Siri AI on HomePod mini and existing Apple TV 4K boxes.

We expect the OS 27.3 beta to begin in the first week of November, with the final release likely arriving in late November or early December.

...

Here are the shows, series, and movies we expect to release on Apple TV+ in November 2026. If you want to know what’s coming later, check our full guide to upcoming Apple TV+ content.

Stick (season 2): A sports comedy about a washed-up ex-pro golfer who coaches a young 17-year-old phenom. November 4

Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook: Hollywood actor and comedian Nora Lum (aka Awkwafina) is the descendant of restaurant royalty … but she can’t cook. Join the star on an inspiring culinary road trip as she learns the craft and attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese eatery. November 6

12 12 12: Each episode of 12 12 12 unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist, and the 12 days following. November 13 (Get it?)

Being Heumann: In 1977, young disabled Judy Heumann and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. What begins as one impulsive act becomes the longest occupation of a federal building in American history, as hundreds spontaneously seize government offices and refuse to leave until the bureaucrat in their way takes action. November 13

Way of the Warrior Kid: Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc, a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything, from academics to P.E.

title: Apple Has Another Product Launch on November 13 | The Apple Post
text:
Apple’s November product launches do not end with the five Macs and iPads arriving on November 6.

Exactly one week later, on Friday, November 13, Apple will launch two more products: the $299 HomeView smart home hub and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K.

The second launch day shifts Apple’s focus away from Mac and iPad and firmly into the living room and smart home.

## Apple HomeView arrives November 13

HomeView is Apple’s new shared smart home display, combining a 7-inch Liquid Retina screen with Siri AI, FaceTime, Apple Home controls, entertainment, and personalized experiences for different members of a household.

The tabletop HomeView and wall-mounted version both start at $299 in the United States, while the standard model costs £299 in the United Kingdom. The Apple Post has a full guide to everything HomeView can do.

HomeView is also central to Apple’s wider smart home push. It can show compatible camera feeds, control lights, locks, thermostats, and other accessories, and work with the new Apple Home Collection arriving from December. Our launch coverage looks at how HomeView fits into Apple’s new home strategy.

## New Apple TV 4K launches the same day

The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K also goes on sale November 13, priced at $299 in the U.S. and £299 in the UK.

It introduces the A19 chip, three far-field microphones for hands-free Siri, Siri AI, a new Siri Remote with Precision Finding, and support for a four-speaker surround sound setup using compatible HomePod models. Here is everything you need to know about the new Apple TV 4K.

Both HomeView and Apple TV 4K have been available to pre-order since October 13, although some delivery estimates began slipping beyond launch day shortly after pre-orders opened.

Apple confirms both products officially become available on Friday, November 13. Apple’s HomeView announcement and Apple TV 4K announcement detail the launch timing.

title: Apple news this week: touchscreen Macs arrive, Duo still scarce - Australian Apple News
text:
Posted on November 9, 2026 November 12, 2026 

A busy week. Five new devices went on sale in Australia on Friday, John Ternus delivered his first earnings as CEO, and the first iOS 27.3 betas arrived with a few changes worth noting.

## New Macs and an OLED iPad mini are here

Image: Apple

Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro is now on sale here, alongside a 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, an M6 iMac and a redesigned iPad mini.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display — a tandem OLED panel with touch — starts at $4,599, and the 16-inch model starts at $5,499. A separate 14-inch model with M6, and the familiar Liquid Retina XDR display, starts at $3,199. The 24-inch iMac with M6 starts at $2,399. The new iPad mini has an 8.5-inch OLED display and an A20 Pro chip; Wi-Fi models start at $1,099, and Wi-Fi + Cellular at $1,349. Prices include GST.

...

Apple reported September-quarter revenue of US$114.5 billion, up 12 per cent, in John Ternus’s first results since he took over on 1 September. Earnings per share were US$2.10, up 14 per cent. Fiscal 2026 revenue hit an all-time high of US$479 billion, with a September-quarter record for iPhone and an all-time high for Services. Mac revenue was US$10.8 billion, up 24 per cent, and Ternus said Apple has “never sold more Macs in a fiscal year” than it did in 2026.

The iPhone Duo is a different story. It went on sale on 23 October, so it barely figures in these numbers, and supply is still tight. “Duo is constrained as of today,” Ternus told Reuters. “We’re not able to predict when supply and demand will be in balance.” He also said a “very small percentage” of units had been returned over display issues. If you’ve been waiting on a Duo in Australia, there’s still no date to plan around.

## iOS 27.3 heads into beta

Apple released the first developer betas of iOS 27.3 and the rest of the 27.3 family on Tuesday, with public betas on Thursday. The public releases are expected in December.

It’s the biggest update to iOS 27 since September. Safari gets a vertical tabs option and an Adaptive Dark Mode for sites that don’t offer their own. Siri AI can do more in Apple’s apps, and the redesigned Health app is back, with custom Insights and longevity information. macOS 27.3 also brings Live Activities to Macs that don’t have a Dynamic Island.

From 27.3, photos and files you share from iCloud with “Anyone with the link” will be “made accessible to Apple” for a harmful-content check. Links limited to people you choose, and “Send a Copy”, are not included. Apple says content shared with anyone is no longer end-to-end encrypted, even if Advanced Data Protection is on.

## Dating apps, and AI companions, headed for 18+

On Monday, Apple told developers that from 16 November they will need to declare whether an app shares real-world location, or includes dating and relationship features — including virtual companions that engage in sexual or romantic content. Apps in that dating category will get a minimum age rating of 18+. Developers have until 12 January 2027 to complete the declarations.

## What to watch next week

HomeView, Apple’s new smart home hub, and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K are due on sale on Friday, 13 November. A minor software update, iOS 27.2.1, arrived on Monday with fixes for iMessage group chats and Bluetooth pairing. If you haven’t installed it yet, it’s worth doing.
